references.text: The claim that Jesus is "the Holy One of God" (ἅγιος τοῦ θεοῦ) has a strong parallel in Psalm 89:19, where God is referred to as "the Holy One of Israel," a title later transferred to Jesus in the NT.
Psalm 16:10 uses the term "your holy one" (ἅγιος) regarding the Messiah, which connects to Peter's confession in [ref:Acts 2:27|Acts 2:27] and Jesus' identity as the Holy One from God.
Peter's confession in Matt 16:16 is the direct parallel to John 6:69, where he identifies Jesus as "the Son of the living God," a confession built on the same revelation.
The demon in Mark 1:24 recognizes Jesus as "the Holy One of God," a title that emphasizes his divine origin and holy nature, just as the disciples confess in John 6:69.
Luke 4:34 repeats the title "the Holy One of God" from the Gospel of Mark, linking Jesus to the plan of the holy God, which is the core of the disciples' faith in John 6:69.
Peter refers to Jesus as "the Holy and Righteous One" in [ref:Acts 3:14|Acts 3:14], a direct reference to the title used in John 6:69.
